transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-11-09 16:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Morgan (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Claire (Redwood Solutions), Ethan (Redwood CSM), Aisha (Pinecrest Procurement), Devon (Security), Marcus (Finance), Rita (Legal)

Summary: quick kickoff between procurement/legal and Redwood to align contract and billing items ahead of pilot.

00:00:03 Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, I think we have about an hour, I'll kick off, quick intro from our side then hear priorities from Pinecrest.
00:00:12 Aisha: Thanks Morgan, appreciate it. I'm Aisha, Head of Procurement, we coordinate legal and billing. Main things: MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA levels for pilot, and how billing/egress shows up to our P&L.
00:00:25 Morgan: Totally, that's the plan. Samir and Claire will cover technical guardrails and security artifacts and then we'll go through the MSA items you flagged in the intake.
00:00:34 Samir: Hi all, Samir here, I'll do the latency/capacity and fallback explanation. Quick note: Redwood serves models across hosted, dedicated, and private - behavior differs a bit.
00:00:46 Devon: Sorry to interrupt, can you define dedicated vs hosted again? We flagged a few items around data residency and key management.
00:00:52 Samir: Sure, dedicated is reserved GPU capacity for your tenant, predictable throughput. Hosted is shared infra with isolation at the tenant layer and lower cost but less guaranteed throughput. Private is customer-managed VPC or on-prem. Key mgmt: we integrate with KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated; hosted can use customer-managed keys via BYOK with some restrictions.
00:01:15 Rita: On MSA redlines, there are three big asks: stronger indemnity carveouts, stricter data deletion language in DPA, and clearer SLA credits. Marcus will look at billing timing.
00:01:25 Marcus: For finance, the egress and token billing assumptions need to be explicit - and the pilot must be within a capped spend or we won't start.
00:01:33 Morgan: That makes sense. For pricing we usually offer a pilot cap and then a transition to either usage-based or reserved monthly commits. We'll put that into the spreadsheet.
00:01:44 Claire: I'll jump in on security artifacts we can provide: SOC2 Type II, encryption at rest and in transit, audit logs, and architecture diagram for Private deployment.
00:01:56 Devon: Great. For audit logs, do you retain token-level traces? We need to know retention windows and redaction options.
00:02:05 Claire: By default logs are retained 90 days in hosted; Dedicated/Private can be configured longer or forwarded to customer SIEM. Token-level traces can be redacted or hashed depending on your classification.
00:02:18 Aisha: Ok, that's good to know. Rita, any immediate legal blockers?
00:02:22 Rita: The indemnity and limitation of liability sections — we usually need them aligned with our vendor policy. Also we're pushing for a data residency and deletion SLA in the DPA; currently language is a bit vague.
00:02:34 Morgan: Understood. We can send a redline matrix showing Redwood's responses to each clause. We'll also propose alternative phrasing for the deletion SLA with timeboxes.
00:02:44 Aisha: Timeline: we need the legal loop closed in two weeks to keep our pilot start date. Is that feasible?
00:02:50 Morgan: Two weeks is tight but doable — provided we get your consolidated redlines in 3-4 working days.
00:02:58 Rita: We can aim for that but need to loop in corporate counsel — may be tight.
00:03:04 Samir: On SLA tiering — here's the practical tradeoff: lower latency and higher availability require Dedicated or Private; hosted can meet baseline SLOs but you won't get the same tail-latency guarantees. We also have fallback policies where requests route to a compatible model variant if capacity is constrained.
00:03:22 Devon: That fallback is a concern for us — how is it surfaced to the app? Is there an explicit header or signal? We can't silently drop to a cheaper model for PII workloads.
00:03:31 Samir: Good point. We expose routing metadata and can enforce model pinning for sensitive workloads; you can do strict routing to Private or Dedicated for those calls. Fallback policies are configurable per-route.
00:03:44 Marcus: Billing question: how do we separate egress charges from inference? We need a clean line for internal chargebacks.
00:03:51 Ethan: We provide per-token and per-embedding metering plus a separate egress bandwidth charge on Hosted. For Dedicated we can include egress in the reserved price or itemize it; open to what works for Pinecrest.
00:04:05 Marcus: Prefer itemized so we can allocate to network costs. Also monthly vs net-45?
00:04:11 Morgan: We typically bill monthly on net-30 for self-serve; enterprise can be net-45 or net-60 — we can flag this as a commercial negotiation item. We'll note it in the pricing sheet.
00:04:22 Aisha: Pilot spend cap — can Redwood put a hard cap with overage alerts? We need that to approve pilot.
00:04:29 Morgan: Yes, we can set caps and alerts. For hosted we can gating the API key, and for Dedicated we can set quota enforcement. We'll codify it in the pilot SOW.
00:04:39 Rita: Any escrow or break-glass for data access? We need clarity if Redwood can access logs, and under what legal process.
00:04:47 Claire: Support engineers have access under strict policies; access is audited. For Private deployments, access can be disabled except via customer approval. We'll include personnel lists and escalation processes in the artifacts.
00:04:58 Devon: Encryption keys — for hosted BYOK is supported but there are caveats?
00:05:03 Samir: Yes, BYOK for hosted supports envelope encryption; however, dedicated/private supports direct HSM integration with full customer key control. We'll spell out constraints.
00:05:13 Aisha: On SLA credits — we need specific credit calculations tied to availability windows, not just 'reasonable efforts'. Can you propose numbers?
00:05:21 Morgan: Absolutely. Typical SLA tiers we propose: 99.9% availability with partial credit structure, 99.95% for Dedicated with higher credits, and 99.99% for Private with elevated remedies. We'll send the exact matrix.
00:05:35 Rita: We won't accept unlimited liability but need clarity around cap and exclusions. Also, the data breach remediation responsibilities need to be explicit.
00:05:43 Morgan: We'll present a couple of liability caps options aligned to enterprise norms; also propose faster incident response SLAs for security incidents as a concession.
00:05:53 Devon: Do you support SOC 2 continuous monitoring or a snapshot report only?
00:05:58 Claire: SOC2 Type II annual with quarterly attestations on select controls; for higher assurance we can do a custom attestation with an expanded scope as part of an enterprise contract.
00:06:10 Marcus: On pricing bands — do you have volume discounts or commit tiers for inference?
00:06:15 Morgan: Yes, volume tiers and reserved capacity discounts; we can model a blended price for token-heavy workloads and separate reserved GPU pool pricing for Dedicated. We'll include sample models in the spreadsheet.
00:06:25 Aisha: Anything about data residency? We operate in EU and want data to remain in EU. How do you support that?
00:06:33 Samir: We have region-specific deployment options; Hosted will route to EU region, Dedicated/Private can be provisioned in EU data centers. We'll note egress across regions and potential transfer fees.
00:06:45 Rita: On deletion SLA — we need 'within X days' language with certification of deletion. Is that doable?
00:06:51 Claire: Yes, we can commit to deletion within 30 days for customer content and provide a deletion certificate. For cached prefixes there are specifics we'll outline.
00:07:02 Morgan: Ok want to walk through next steps: we'll send the redline matrix, SOC2, architecture and sample pricing. Samir will add a short technical note on fallback and model pinning.
00:07:12 Aisha: We'll try to consolidate redlines quickly. If we can get to agreement by 11/23 we can start pilot in early December.
00:07:20 Morgan: Sounds good. Any other open topics?
00:07:24 Devon: Just one — can we run a small benchmark for latency and tail-p99 with a 1k token sequence? We need numbers to compare with our in-house.
00:07:33 Samir: Yes, we can run an e2e benchmark. We'll propose a test harness and sample prompt set; need your test account and keys.
00:07:42 Marcus: And we'll need pricing for the benchmark run; can that be included in the pilot cap?
00:07:47 Morgan: Yep, we'll include the benchmark cost in the pilot cap.
00:07:52 Rita: Ok final ask — can Redwood provide contact for security incident manager? We want a named point-of-contact for legal escalation.
00:07:58 Claire: I'll include that contact and escalation ladder in the artifacts.
00:08:03 Morgan: Great — recap: Redwood to send MSA redline matrix, pricing sheet with pilot cap options, SOC2 and architecture docs, tech note on fallback, and benchmark plan. Pinecrest to consolidate redlines and confirm timeline.
00:08:17 Aisha: Thanks all. We'll aim to get redlines back by Tuesday 11/16.
00:08:22 Morgan: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the legal deep-dive and send the artifacts today.
00:08:28 End of recording.
